evals.name: review-the-current-diff
evals.setup: A staged diff that drops one error return and wraps another with `fmt.Errorf` using `%v` instead of `%w`. Nothing names a target.
expected_behavior: Resolves the target to the current diff and lists the files in scope
Reasons only — runs no gofmt, vet, linter, or `go test`
Invokes `golang:style` for the style dimension and judges correctness itself
Reads neither `references/fixing.md` nor `references/rule-editing.md`: this is a check run, not a fix or a rule edit
Groups findings Blocker / Should-fix / Nit, each with `file:line`, the rule id or dimension (`style: %w`, `correctness`), and a minimal fix
Ends with a ship / fix-first verdict and per-severity counts

evals.name: broad-target-auto-plan-first
evals.setup: A module of eleven packages. The invocation names no budget and no depth.
expected_behavior: Detects the broad target and switches to plan-first on its own
Proposes the defaults it would use — `max_issues=25`, `depth=standard`, the package list — and stops for approval before the full pass
Past the approval, fans out one subagent per package and merges into one ranked report capped at `max_issues`

evals.name: rule-edit-add-change-remove
evals.setup: `../style/SKILL.md` already carries a receiver-naming rule. The session issues three rule edits in turn.
evals.query: /review add "no naked returns in tests", then /review change "receivers are three letters", then /review remove "the compile-time check rule"
expected_behavior: Recognizes each as a rule edit rather than a review target
Turns the `add` into a terse imperative one-liner in the existing style, scoped to Test
Detects a duplicate or conflicting rule and waits for confirmation before writing to `../style/SKILL.md`, showing the before/after of the rule text
Rewrites the existing receiver-naming line in place for the `change` instead of adding a second rule
For the `remove`, deletes the `../style/SKILL.md` line plus its keyed `../style/rules.md` entry and Contents row, after confirmation

evals.name: learn-from-the-session
evals.setup: A finished session in which the user renamed a helper for clarity, asked to convert an `f(p *T)` function into a method, and separately asked for a one-off rename specific to this project's domain.
expected_behavior: Scans the session's Go feedback and pairs each item with the diff hunk that resolved it
Proposes only the generalizable rules — method-over-func, behaviour-named helper — each with its provenance and a before/after example
Drops the task-specific one-off and dedupes against the rules `../style/SKILL.md` already carries
Waits for the user to pick before writing; on confirmation writes the `../style/SKILL.md` line plus its keyed `../style/rules.md` entry and shows the diff

evals.name: broad-fix-job-plans-and-pauses
evals.setup: Findings span five packages, one of them large enough to warrant file-level chunks.
expected_behavior: Detects the broad scope and writes an ordered plan to `tmp/review-fix-plan.md` — one chunk per package, findings listed, status boxes — and gets a go-ahead before editing
Splits the large package into file-level chunks
Proves each bug red then green with a test named to `have`/`want`
Runs `go test ./... -race` per chunk so each chunk ends green, ticking the plan boxes as it goes
Pauses after each changed chunk for a go-ahead and never proceeds past an unmade decision
Never runs `git commit` — each chunk lands as a separately committable change

evals.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Opens with the findings — no preamble, no narration of reading the rules
States each finding once and reports budget usage
No closing summary re-listing findings the user can already see
